sermon.title: Powerful Revelations Part 3
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Revelation 4 and 5: the elders bowing before the throne, the sealed scroll that only the Lamb is worthy to open, and the heavenly worship of Jesus Christ. He teaches that believers are made kings and priests to rule over sin, that praise reminds us who God is, and that the sevens of Revelation point to what is coming.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he reads Revelation 4:8–5:14 without naming the chapters and verses (verse 13 is named at about 11:37), so those references are editorial; “Mary of old” (about 20:27) alludes to Luke 1:45. Several words were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear] (about 0:15, 1:55, 4:32, 12:33, 15:19, 16:00, 17:16). The remarks on other religions’ founders and religious leaders (about 11:00), the Catholic Church’s bowing (about 12:00), recovery programs and counseling (about 8:00 and 18:55), and a church split (about 19:27) reflect his views as preached.

He’s the crown of crowns. Anything you got is really unworthy of what he’s done. So here they are bowing. So you want to know what’s going on in heaven? You’re getting a picture of it. chunks.section_question: What does he say the sealed scroll shows about messengers? (Revelation 5:1–4)
chunks.short_answer: He explains that “a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book,” and that “the messenger who took it could open it, but he wasn’t what? Worthy.” He says “we are messengers. Only Jesus can open the book to people.”
chunks.text:
Whoa. “I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a scroll written inside and out, sealed with seven seals.” See, there’s that scroll. Now, a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book and had the symbol of the one who sent the message. And no one could open it but the one, the one who sent the message gave authority to open it. You understand that it wasn’t locks on there, you know, wasn’t chains. It was just a seal. Anybody could open it. The messenger who took it could open it, but he wasn’t what? Worthy. He didn’t have the authority. The messenger, and that’s what pastors and priests and ministers got to understand.

We are messengers. Only Jesus can open the book to people. Only Jesus can open their understanding. Only Jesus can do this stuff. Amen. That’s good. So, we see the one on the throne and we see that sardius and jasper, an emerald rainbow there, and another artist’s drawing of it. “Then I saw a strong [unclear] proclaiming with a loud voice, ‘Who is worthy to open the scroll and to loose its seals?’ And no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look at it. So I wept much because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll or to look in it.”

chunks.section_question: What does he say about the Lion and the Lamb who open the scroll? (Revelation 5:5–10)
chunks.short_answer: He reads “the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll,” and “a lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God.” He says “if they’re worshiping in heaven, don’t you think we ought to get warmed up here on earth?”
chunks.text:
“But one of the elders,” hey, hallelujah, the elders are coming through here, “one of the elders said to me, ‘Don’t weep. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.’” So, we got a scroll with seven seals. We got a lamb slain that was worthy to open the scroll. “And then I looked, and in the midst of the throne, the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders stood a lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God.” He keeps talking about these seven spirits of God. “And he came and took the scroll out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne. And when he had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the 24 elders fell down before the lamb.

Here they are again, each having a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying, ‘You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals. For you were slain and have redeemed us to God by your blood, out of every tribe, tongue, people, and nation.’” Hallelujah. If they’re worshiping in heaven, don’t you think we ought to get warmed up here on earth? If elders, leaders are bowing before him in heaven and casting their rewards before him, don’t you think we need to start now? Am I talking to the wrong people?

chunks.section_question: What does he say believers were made to do? (Revelation 5:10, Ephesians 2:8–9)
chunks.short_answer: He says “I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin. That is his objective.” He adds “you got to pursue Christ and he will work these things in you,” and asks “how many want to rule over sex and drugs and sin and alcohol.”
chunks.text:
But see, we’ve been taught to come and let the preacher do everything for us, or the priest, or whatever. But we are to come and be partakers of these things. And look at this: “You have made us” what? “Kings and priests to reign” where? “To reign” where? See, drugs don’t get me down. Alcohol doesn’t get me down. Sexual permissive does. Why? I was made by Jesus not to be just a fisher of men. Not to be just a believer. Not just to be a person of faith. I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin. That is his objective. Are you with me, church? But you see, when we get bombarded, well, we’re saved by grace through faith and not of works, lest any man should boast.

We don’t, we, we, we just get, uh, uh, pleased with where we’re at. “I don’t have to do nothing.” Yes, you got to pursue Christ and he will work these things in you. Amen. How many want to rule over sex and drugs and sin and alcohol and all that stuff that destroys homes and families and lives? Amen. Yes, Jesus promised to make you a ruler. Alcoholics Anonymous, they got some kind of, you know, uh, what do they call that? What? Higher power. Higher power. Listen, don’t call Jesus a higher power. Call him who he is: Jesus Christ. Amen. He’s the one that has the power to cause you to be a ruler here on earth.

chunks.section_question: Who does he say is praised in heaven? (Revelation 5:11–13)
chunks.short_answer: He reads “worthy is the lamb who was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and glory and honor and blessing,” and says that in heaven it is Jesus Christ who is honored, not any founder or religious leader. He says “remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ.”
chunks.text:
It worked in my life. It worked in a slew of others that I grew up with, and they’re here today and still serving God. And it will work for you. And his name is Jesus, and the book is the Bible. Hallelujah. This stuff works. Now, he goes on to say, uh, I think I just passed up something. “Then I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. And the number of them was 10,000 times 10 thousands and thousands of thousands.” In other words, over a 100 million angels are up there. Plus “saying with a loud voice, ‘Worthy is the lamb who was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and glory and honor and blessing.’” You notice it’s not Allah.

It’s not Muhammad. It’s not Joseph Smith. They’re up there honoring. Who is it? Jesus Christ. Is not Mary Baker Eddy or any Pope Benedict or a pope of any kind or Billy Graham or some evangelist in a Protestant church. It is Jesus Christ. And folks, if it is Jesus Christ in the eternities, then we need to start what? Worshiping him, seeking him and acknowledging him now. Amen. Remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. chunks.section_question: Why does he say bowing and worship matter now?
chunks.short_answer: He says “up there, the very power of his presence is going to put you on your face,” and that God uses bowing because “in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power.” He says of bowing, “it’s not unhealthy… your spirit is going to be strengthened.”
chunks.text:
Man, they’re just up and down. That’s one thing I like about the Catholic Church. They bow a lot. And Protestants could use some of that. They get on their knees and it’s scriptural. So now it’s not just the elders, but everyone on earth, under the earth, are dead people up there. We’re all going to be what? Worshiping him. And you’re not going to say, “Well, I didn’t grow up that way. Well, I was timid. I, I can’t do this. I’m [unclear].” No. Up there, the very power of his presence is going to put you on your face. And why does, why does the Bible give us the bowing thing? Because in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power.

When people would go into a natural king, they would what? Bow. A given recognition that you are a higher power than I am. And so God used it. He speaks to us in natural things so we can understand spiritual things. And does it hurt us to humble ourselves and bow and lift up our voice? No, it doesn’t do anything. It’s not unhealthy. You’re not going to have a heart attack. You know, uh, it’s not going to affect you in any way except your spirit is going to be strengthened. See, he chose the humble way. We humble ourselves and do these things. See, you want to, this is a little picture of what you’ve been doing in heaven. This is not the total picture, but there’s a little glimpse. There’s more. Remember, Jesus didn’t make us just fishers of men. Not just believers, not just people of faith, but kings and priests to rule on earth, to rule over the kingdom of darkness, to rule over Satan and Satan’s children who follow evil.

chunks.section_question: Does he say God needs to be told how great he is?
chunks.short_answer: He says “he don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is,” and “you’re not telling God anything.” He says “he ordained praise and worship for you to give to him so you are reminded who he is,” and “then your faith is built up to possess the things that he told you you could have.”
chunks.text:
Even family members who want to lead us astray. You see, now let me explain. Some people say, “Well, what kind of God is up there with a big ego? He wants to be told how great he is.” He don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is. You’re not telling God anything. Get off your hobby horse. But you see, you need to remember who he is. See, this is what affects your thinking. This is what affects your spirit. You need to remember who he is. And so he ordained praise and worship for you to give to him so you are reminded who he is. And then your faith is built up to possess the things that he told you you could have. Does that make sense? And it brings his presence.

He comes and touches us and refreshes us in that, and we get our mind changed and we get our spirit refreshed when we worship and praise and seek the Lord our God. That make sense? Yeah. He’s not up there wanting, “Come on, praise me. Come on, praise.” No. Ministers like that. Preachers like people to slap him on the back and say, “What a good message.” [unclear]. “Oh man, what, what a man you are, a woman you are.” No, no, no. Jesus is in my, he already knows who he is. He doesn’t have to be told. But you need to know. See, I can’t get into praise and say anything bad about Jesus. When I start lifting up his name, I have to start saying, “Lord, you’re the creator of the world.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about the past and about boasting? (Psalm 25:7, 2 Corinthians 5:17)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the blood of Jesus healed my past. He does not remember the sins of my youth,” and “I’m a new creature.” He says “praise means to boast about,” and that “even if I attain something in God, I have to recognize it was him who did it.”
chunks.text: I don’t have to go back to the past and try to get cleansed of some kind of stupid healing thing that they have. The blood of Jesus healed my past. He does not remember the sins of my youth. Don’t talk about my past. It’s dead. I’m a new creature. Are you with me? See, this is what praise: praise means to boast about. You can’t boast about yourself. The Bible says if you boast of yourself, your boasting is wrong. Let others boast of you. And there’s nothing in me to boast about. You’ve seen these elders casting their crowns before him. Even if I attain something in God, I have to recognize it was him who did it. And just give it back. Amen. Are you with me? Now, isn’t that powerful?

chunks.section_question: What does he say about seeking Jesus instead of paying for counseling? (Matthew 7:7)
chunks.short_answer: He says “this is not a religion. This is a reality. Jesus is real,” and that people “will pay 50 bucks an hour for counseling from some psychologist and won’t get on their knees for that half hour with the Bible.” He says “I started at age 20 and haven’t stopped yet. I never backslid, never had a nervous breakdown.”
chunks.text: And this is the Jesus that we have. There’s no other religion on earth that promises you these things, folks, because they’re man-made religions. This is not a religion. This is a reality. Jesus is real. And the Bible says if you will seek and keep seeking and ask and keep asking and knock and keep knocking. I am just amazed at how people will pay 50 bucks an hour for counseling from some psychologist and won’t get on their knees for that half hour with the Bible and seek him who has the power to change their thinking, to change their emotions, to change their spirit. I’m just shocked, and it worked for me.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about church splits and Christ being formed in us? (Galatians 4:19, Luke 1:45)
chunks.short_answer: He says he “didn’t fall apart when the church split because it wasn’t my church. It’s his church.” He says “Christ is still wanting to form himself in his church,” and that Jesus “come to give us a sound mind, strong emotions, a strong spirit.”
chunks.text:
I started at age 20 and haven’t stopped yet. I never backslid, never had a nervous breakdown. I didn’t fall apart when the church split because it wasn’t my church. It’s his church. If people want to leave Christ in his church, then Christ can deal with them. It’s not my problem. Are you out there? But shouldn’t you feel bad? No. It’s not my church. It’s not my problem. If people want to go, I say bye. I go on following Christ. Isn’t that what Jesus said to do? Just keep following him. Isn’t it shocking in America that people are going from church to church and can’t handle the least adversity and flaw in a church, and we’ve been offered this Jesus who is so powerful and so great.

Are you with me? Don’t you think it’s time that we go God like Mary of old: “Let there be a performance of that which was spoken.” You know she birthed Jesus, and the Bible says, Paul says, we travail in Christ, we travail again that Christ would be formed in you. See it, we, Christ is still wanting to form himself in his church. And Christians have mental breakdowns and mental problems and emotional problems when Jesus did not come to leave us in that condition. And he come to give us a sound mind, strong emotions, a strong spirit. And so don’t give up on yourself. Yes, you’ve made mistakes in the past, but the Bible says he won’t remember the sins of your youth.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about the sevens in Revelation and “7777”?
chunks.short_answer: He says “let the blood shut the door,” and “give God some time. He can’t lie. He has to do what he said he would do.” He closes by listing seven churches, seven candlesticks, seven spirits and more, and says “that’s what’s coming. 7777, not 666.”
chunks.text: Let the blood shut the door. They’re done. If you’ve asked for repentance, it’s done. You’re a new creature. Let’s start a fresh and a new and give God time to work his image and his inheritance in you. Now, that’s a good place for an amen. Give God some time. He can’t lie. He has to do what he said he would do. Seven churches, seven candlesticks, seven spirits, seven lamps, seven horns, seven eyes, seven stars, seven messengers, seven angels, seven seals, seven trumpets, seven thunders, seven plagues. That’s what’s coming. 7777, not 666.

faqs.question: What does he say a seal was?
faqs.answer: He says “a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book and had the symbol of the one who sent the message.”

faqs.question: Who does he say is worthy to open the scroll?
faqs.answer: He reads that “the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals,” and that a lamb “was worthy to open the scroll.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.”

faqs.answer: He says “I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin.”

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus should be called a “higher power”?

faqs.question: What does he say about counseling and step programs?
faqs.answer: He says “it amazes me how people will go to counseling and seven-step procedures and 12-step procedures and all the rest and won’t go to Jesus and his word.”

faqs.answer: He says it is Jesus Christ, and “remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ.”

faqs.answer: He says “in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power,” and “he speaks to us in natural things so we can understand spiritual things.”

faqs.question: Does he say God needs praise to feel great?
faqs.answer: No. He says “he don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is,” but “you need to remember who he is.”

faqs.question: Does he say God remembers the sins of our youth?
faqs.answer: No. He says “he does not remember the sins of my youth,” and “the blood of Jesus healed my past.”
